issues.p: BioFlo PICC lines (6 codes)
issues.s: Temporary discontinuation while a new manufacturer awaits certification; delisted Jun/Jul 2026, resolution expected 01/12/2026.
issues.use: Trusts using BioFlo PICCs need an alternative until at least December 2026 — a live opening for other PICC suppliers.

issues.p: Venflon IV cannula with wings, 14G–22G
issues.s: Discontinued through rationalisation; progressive delisting since Jan 2025, all codes delisted by 31/07/2026.
issues.use: Any trust still on Venflon must convert now — an immediate switching conversation for every cannula supplier.

issues.p: 4Fr single-lumen PowerPICC (SOLO and non-SOLO)
issues.s: Global product removal for material-fatigue leak risk (FSN updated 15/05/2025); unused stock destroyed.
issues.use: Context for PICC conversations — ask what the trust moved to and whether the replacement is bedding in well.

issues.p: Cook FSN covering several sets, including the Spectrum Central Venous Catheter Set
issues.s: Field safety notice dated 05/03/2026 (MHRA ref 38698628) listing multiple Cook products including the Spectrum Central Venous Catheter Set; the MHRA listing does not state the nature of the issue — read the FSN itself before quoting it.
issues.use: A live Cook FSN touches the Spectrum central venous catheter set — ask your central line accounts whether they were affected and what action they took, without assuming the fault.

issues.p: Disposable Infusion Set (A211M, A211M1F, A211M5F1, A311M, A311M021F, A212)
issues.s: Field safety notice dated 01/07/2026 (MHRA ref 40179552), listed on the MHRA's 13–17 July 2026 FSN page; the listing does not state the nature of the issue — read the FSN itself before quoting it. The same page also lists a Medtronic Sphere-360 catheter FSN (ref 40194215).
issues.use: An open field safety notice on a disposable infusion set is a reason to ask your infusion accounts whether they hold Medcaptain stock and what they would move to, without assuming the fault.

issues.p: Supply Issues Salter Labs UK T/A Airlife Nasal Cannula and Oxygen Facemask Products FDK6925 and FDK6926 (ICN 3179)
issues.s: Auto-detected from NHS Supply Chain ICN - open the source for details and verify before use.

issues.p: Interventional urology portfolio (110 NHS Supply Chain lines)
issues.s: Field Safety Notice 16/12/2024: withdrawal over possible sterility issue; 42 lines suspended, 3 permanently deactivated.
issues.use: Ask which lines your accounts lost and whether replacements have fully restored service.

issues.p: Rüsch self-retaining (Foley) and intermittent catheters
issues.s: Ongoing supply issue; seven codes still suspended as of May 2026; 12 PTFE-coated Foley lines discontinued and delisted.
issues.use: Affected trusts need alternative Foley supply now — a direct opening for other indwelling-catheter suppliers.

issues.p: Wellead 2-way silicone Foley catheters
issues.s: Wellead range delisted from 01/05/2026; Folysil reinstated as the sole Coloplast silicone Foley option.
issues.use: Trusts that used Wellead have just changed product — worth asking how the transition has gone.

issues.p: NephroMax high pressure nephrostomy balloon catheters (eight affected product codes)
issues.s: NHS Supply Chain field safety notice (ICN 3416) dated 22/07/2026: the renal sheath on affected lots may be packaged in a reversed orientation, and if this is not corrected before use the non-tapered end may be inserted in the patient, which could increase resistance and result in difficulty advancing, withdrawing or positioning the catheter. The eight affected products remain available via eDirect; users are told to verify sheath orientation before use and correct it if necessary, as described in Appendix A of the notice. No alternative product is named.
issues.use: This is a check-before-use correction rather than a withdrawal, so there is no supply gap to fill here. It is still a fair reason to ask your urology and interventional radiology accounts whether the notice has reached the people actually opening the packs.

issues.p: Convatec EsteemBody one-piece intestinal ostomy bag, open-ended (MHRA ref 38578479)
issues.s: Field safety notice listed on the MHRA's 16-20 February 2026 FSN page (Convatec EsteemBody, one-piece intestinal ostomy bag, open-ended, ref 38578479); the listing does not state the nature of the issue - read the FSN itself before quoting it. The same page also lists a Merit Medical 16F Dual-Valved Splittable Sheath Introducer FSN (ref 38519371), which is vascular access rather than continence.
issues.use: An open field safety notice on a one-piece ostomy bag is a reason to ask your stoma care accounts whether they hold EsteemBody stock and what they would move to, without assuming the fault.

issues.p: ChloraPrep 2% applicators and the procedure packs containing them: NPC codes DMK000 (1ml), MRB303 (1.5ml), MRB306 (3ml) and MRB494 (3ml tinted)
issues.s: NHS Supply Chain ICN 3359, latest update 28/07/2026: MHRA recall for a potential breach of sterility in the packaging process, expanded to all lot numbers with an expiry date up to and including 05/2029. Trusts are told to cease use and quarantine all affected products, and to return stocked items by Friday 14 August 2026 — except Rocialle stocked products, where the notice states 'All goods to be returned no later than Friday 7 August 2026' using reason code 7. Procedure packs from B Braun, Unisurge, Rocialle Healthcare and Kimal are also caught.
issues.use: The same sterility recall as ICN 3355, widened to the procedure packs that contain ChloraPrep. Every account that preps a line is quarantining stock and returning it, so ask what they are prepping with in the meantime and whether that stand-in is likely to stick. Check the deadline that actually applies to them: Rocialle stocked products are due back by 7 August 2026, everything else by 14 August 2026. Worth checking procedure-pack users too, not just applicator users. For what it has done to availability, see ICN 3397.

issues.p: Cannulation packs, 13 product codes (full list in the notice's attachment)
issues.s: NHS Supply Chain notice 28/07/2026: all 13 affected codes are suspended and unavailable to order, caused by a component shortage and by the recall on ChloraPrep, which is a component in these packs. NHS Supply Chain states there are no alternatives available and anticipates the supply issue will be resolved by 31 August 2026.
issues.use: Thirteen B Braun cannulation pack codes are off the shelf until the end of August with no alternative listed, so ask cannulation accounts how they are covering the gap and whether your own pack or the individual components can fill it. This is a knock on from the ChloraPrep sterility recall in ICN 3359, which caught the applicators inside these packs, so treat the two as one conversation rather than two.

issues.p: Supply Issues PDI (EMEA) Ltd Skin Disinfectant Biocide DEC85019 (ICN 3423)
issues.s: Auto-detected from NHS Supply Chain ICN - open the source for details and verify before use.

issues.p: ChloraPrep 2% w/v / 70% v/v cutaneous solution, 1mL applicators
issues.s: Class 2 medicines recall issued 13/07/2026 (EL(26)A/34) for a potential breach of sterility in the packaging process; covers the listed lots with expiry dates up to and including 05/2029, with stock to be quarantined and returned to suppliers.
issues.use: ChloraPrep sterility recall, notice 3 of 4. The 13/07/2026 Class 2 recall that widened the same packaging defect to every lot expiring up to and including 05/2029. This is the MHRA's version of the scope NHS Supply Chain then applied to the procedure packs in ICN 3359. Line insertion accounts have had their 1mL applicators pulled, so ask what they are prepping with now and whether that stand in is going to stick.

issues.p: ChloraPrep 2% 1mL and ChloraPrep Frepp 2% 1.5mL applicators
issues.s: Class 2 medicines recall issued 02/06/2026 (EL(26)A/26) for a potential breach of sterility in the packaging process, covering batches with expiry dates up to and including 02/2028 (ChloraPrep 1mL) and 01/2028 (ChloraPrep Frepp 1.5mL); a wider recall followed on 13/07/2026.
issues.use: ChloraPrep sterility recall, notice 1 of 4. This is where it started, on 02/06/2026, when the recall still reached only expiry 02/2028 on the 1mL and 01/2028 on the Frepp 1.5mL. Useful for showing an account that this is a three month old problem that has kept widening, not a July one off. It has since been overtaken twice, by EL(26)A/34 on 13/07/2026 and by NHS Supply Chain ICN 3359 at its 28/07/2026 update, so quote the current scope and deadlines from those and not from here.

issues.co: Medline Industries LP and Kimal PLC
issues.p: Namic angiographic control syringes with rotating adaptor, and Namic White Star off-handle manifolds, supplied within Kimal procedure packs
issues.s: MHRA device safety information DSI/2026/002, issued 19/05/2026 and updated 22/05/2026: the rotating adaptor on affected Namic syringes may unscrew during use (risk of disconnection, blood loss, infection and air embolism), and affected manifolds may carry foreign particulates in the fluid pathway; affected products are to be removed and destroyed unless use is unavoidable in an urgent procedure with no alternative.
issues.use: Cath lab and interventional radiology accounts have had recalled components pulled out of their Kimal packs — ask what pack they are running now and whether the substitution has settled.

issues.p: Skin disinfectant applicators DMK000 (1mL, 2% chlorhexidine gluconate) and MRB303 (1.5mL, 2% chlorhexidine gluconate)
issues.s: NHS Supply Chain safety alert (ICN 3355) issued 04/06/2026 and updated 14/07/2026 to extend the affected DMK000 lots to expiry 05/2029; affected stock is to be quarantined and returned no later than 24/07/2026, with MRB306 and MRB494 listed as alternatives subject to each organisation's own clinical suitability review.
issues.use: The original ChloraPrep sterility recall (ICN 3355) — the one most accounts met first. Its 24/07/2026 return deadline has passed but the recall is still open. Two things follow from it, both on this page: it was later widened to the procedure packs containing ChloraPrep (ICN 3359, returns due 7 and 14 August), and the alternatives are now rationed rather than freely available (ICN 3397, to at least 31/10/2026). Ask which code your account actually moved to, because the compliant switch may now be the capped one.

issues.co: Regent Medical Limited / Mölnlycke Health Care
issues.p: Hibiwash 500ml (chlorhexidine gluconate 4%)
issues.s: Class 2 medicines recall issued 23/03/2026 (EL(26)A/15) for microbial contamination (Burkholderia cepacia) found during routine microbiological monitoring at the manufacturing facility; batches 5156042, 5156043 and 5156093 (all expiry 28/11/2028) to be quarantined and returned.
issues.use: A pre-operative skin wash rather than a vascular access or continence product, so background only — but it sits alongside the ChloraPrep recalls as evidence that antiseptic supply has been unsettled this year.

issues.p: FSW288 — needlefree transfer spike take set with Swan-Lock needlefree valve
issues.s: NHS Supply Chain supply issue notice (ICN 3368) dated 16/06/2026, caused by a manufacturing problem at the supplier; FSB399 (needlefree bag spike with SmartSite valve) was offered as an alternative subject to local clinical review, and the notice records the product as available to order again from 15/07/2026.
issues.use: The gap has closed, but accounts that switched to FSB399 in June may not have switched back — worth asking which needlefree connector they are actually using now.

issues.p: FKA321, administration set for the Alaris GP volumetric pump
issues.s: NHS Supply Chain supply issue notice (ICN 3369), most recently updated 22/07/2026: the supply issue is continuing, with shipping delays given as the cause in the 17/06/2026 update. FKA321 is currently suspended and unavailable to order, with resolution expected 20/08/2026. Potential indirect alternatives are listed on the NHS Supply Chain website (login required) and organisations are told to consult their own clinical experts to ensure suitability.
issues.use: Infusion accounts cannot order FKA321 until at least 20 August and are running on indirect alternatives, so ask which set they have moved to and whether their own clinical review has signed it off.

issues.p: ChloraPrep skin disinfectant applicators DMK000, MRB303, MRB306, DMD85004 and DMD85006
issues.s: NHS Supply Chain supply issue notice (ICN 3397) dated 30/06/2026 and updated 24/07/2026 15:39: a temporary pause in production to update the production line, with resolution expected 31/10/2026. At the 24/07/2026 update DMK000 and DMD85004 remain suspended and unavailable, and MRB306, MRB303 and DMD85006 are all subject to Protect Demand Management with daily ordering thresholds. DMD85006 (1.5mL) began delivering into the network from 23/07/2026 and DMD85007 (1.75mL swab stick) from 03/08/2026. The notice records that DMK000 and MRB303 are also affected products on Field Safety Notice ICN 3355, but attributes this supply issue to the production line update, not to the recall.
issues.use: The supply consequence of the ChloraPrep recall (ICN 3355 and 3359), not a separate problem. Skin prep ordering is rationed rather than simply unavailable until at least 31/10/2026, so ask line insertion accounts which codes they can actually get today: with DMK000 and DMD85004 suspended and MRB306 and MRB303 capped by daily thresholds, a trust may be quietly running short even though its usual applicator is still listed.

issues.p: FVP85005, Umbilical Catheter Double Lumen Expert Polyurethane x-ray opaque 4.0 FR 20 CM
issues.s: NHS Supply Chain supply issue notice (ICN 3382) dated 23/06/2026: production was delayed by component availability issues and the product then required an extended sterilisation period before release. FSY028, FSY362 and FVP85003 were offered as alternatives. The 24/07/2026 update states the supply issue with umbilical catheter products from Vygon UK is now resolved.
issues.use: Resolved as of 24/07/2026, so this is a follow up call rather than an open gap: ask neonatal and paediatric accounts that were moved onto FSY028, FSY362 or FVP85003 whether they have gone back to FVP85005 or stayed on the alternative.

issues.p: FAB85002, FWM4155, FWM4157, FWM85015, FWM85047, FWM85062 and FWM85131 - NGPOD enteral feeding device accessories and pH reading device
issues.s: NHS Supply Chain supply issue notice (ICN 3420) dated 28/07/2026: the supply issue is due to reduced manufacturing capabilities. The affected product codes are currently suspended and unavailable to order, and the notice states there are no alternatives available for most of the affected products. Resolution expected 01/09/2026.
issues.use: Enteral feeding rather than vascular access or continence, so background only - but with no alternative for most codes until at least 01/09/2026, it is worth knowing which of your accounts check NG tube placement with NGPOD and are currently stuck.

issues.co: B Braun, Baxter, Becton Dickinson UK Ltd, CODAN, Fannin, GBUK Group Ltd and RPG Medical Ltd
issues.p: IV infusion giving sets and blood transfusion giving sets
issues.s: MHRA Device Safety Information DSI/2026/003, issued 20/05/2026, prompted by a case in which an IV infusion giving set was used instead of a blood transfusion giving set during a neonatal exchange transfusion, causing cardiac arrest and severe brain injury. Using an IV set instead may under-infuse blood or destroy red blood cells (haemolysis). Required actions: store blood transfusion giving sets in clearly labelled containers, in their original packaging, separate from IV infusion giving sets; train staff to tell the two apart; complete a pre-transfusion checklist before starting.
issues.use: This is a storage, labelling and training alert, not a product fault or a recall, so there is no supply gap to sell into. It does open a legitimate conversation about how transfusion sets are stored and distinguished on the ward, and whether clearer packaging or separate storage helps the trust close the actions.

issues.p: balance 2.3% glucose, 1.25 mmol/l calcium, solution for peritoneal dialysis (PL 13689/0013)
issues.s: Class 4 Medicines Defect Notification (DMRC 39439934), issued 14/05/2026: the Braille text on the outer labels incorrectly states 'CAPD/DPCA 19' rather than the correct glucose and calcium composition. Six batches are affected: F4LM071, G4LB133, G4LL144, G4LM152, H4LB212 and G4LI151. The MHRA states there is no product quality issue, the affected batches will not be recalled, and patients may continue to use them. Healthcare professionals should explain the error to visually impaired patients who rely solely on Braille.
issues.use: Low impact and no switching opening: nothing is being recalled and there is no supply gap. It is a fair reason to check in with renal units, who have to flag the Braille error to visually impaired patients themselves.
